docs.description: a state slot is written more than once in one tick with a value-form argument
docs.why: Two value-form writes of the same slot in one tick are both computed from the render-time snapshot, so the second overwrites the first instead of building on it: `setQty(qty + 1); setQty(qty + 1)` adds one, not two. Three limits are worth knowing before acting. The `same_tick` walk is a reachability over-approximation, so two writes on mutually exclusive branches of one handler still match. It does not split on suspension points, so writes separated by an `await` match too (there the intermediate value does render — that is a different smell, an unobservable phase, and usually benign). And `updater` only answers "not a proven function literal", never "this argument reads the slot", because setter-argument positions carry no expression verdict.
docs.fix: Use the functional updater for every write that builds on the current value — `setQty(q => q + 1)` — or collapse the writes into a single call with the final value.
docs.example: const addPair = () => { setQty(qty + 1); setQty(qty + 1); }  // adds one

rules.message: {w.setter} writes {w.slot} in `{w.region}` alongside another write of the same slot in the same tick, and its argument is not a proven functional updater — the writes collapse onto one snapshot

docs.description: an effect exists only to write a state slot it does not itself depend on, on every path
docs.why: An effect whose whole job is `setX(<something built from props and other state>)`, keyed on those inputs, stores derived data in state. The first paint shows the initializer, the effect then forces a second render with the real value, so the user sees a flash and every upstream change costs two renders. The built-in `derived-state` rule only recognises state-mirrors-state; this rule also reaches the prop-derived case. Because the vocabulary cannot ask whether the slot has a *non*-effect writer, a slot that is also edited by a handler (seeded editable state, a legitimate pattern) still matches — check the slot's other writers before acting.
docs.fix: Delete the slot and compute the value during render (`const full = `${first} ${last}``), wrapping it in `useMemo` only if it is genuinely expensive.

rules.message: this effect writes {w.slot} on every path from inputs it declares as deps — derive the value during render instead of mirroring it into state

docs.description: a re-runnable effect starts a one-shot async continuation and returns no cleanup
docs.why: An effect with a non-empty deps array runs again whenever a dep moves, so two continuations can be in flight at once. Without a cleanup nothing invalidates the older one, and whichever response lands last wins — the results list shows matches for a query the user already replaced. The same write also lands after unmount. The built-in `missing-cleanup` rule deliberately skips one-shot registrars (`.then`, `setTimeout`), so this shape has no native cover. `registers` is a registrar-name match, not a proof the callee is the host primitive.
docs.fix: Return a cleanup that invalidates the continuation: flip a captured `let current = true` flag and test it before writing, or abort with an `AbortController` whose signal is passed to the request.

rules.message: this effect re-runs on its deps and starts a one-shot async callback with no cleanup — an older response can resolve last and overwrite the newer one
